images.title: Choose a big enough radius
images.purpose: Contrast a radius less than half of XY, where the arcs never meet, with a radius more than half, where they meet and give the bisector.
images.composition: Two equal panels side by side with a wide gap between them; the left panel shows the failed attempt, the right panel the finished construction.
exact_structure: Left panel: a horizontal dark segment XY, labels X and Y; a grey (#6B7280) arc centred at X and a grey (#6B7280) arc centred at Y, each with radius about one third of XY, drawn above and below XY; the two arcs do not touch, leaving a clear gap in the middle.
Left panel: one small vermilion (#D55E00) cross mark in the gap between the arcs.

Right panel: a horizontal dark segment XY of the same length, labels X and Y; a grey (#6B7280) arc centred at X and a grey (#6B7280) arc centred at Y, each with the same radius of about two thirds of XY, crossing above XY at A and below XY at B.
Right panel: a reddish purple (#CC79A7) line through A and B crossing XY at its midpoint, with a small square right angle mark.
Under the left panel one short caption; under the right panel one short caption.
The labels X and Y appear once in each panel (twice each in all); A and B appear only in the right panel.
rejection: the left panel arcs touching or crossing
the right panel arcs from X and from Y drawn with visibly different radii
the two panels showing segments XY of different lengths
different radii drawn above and below XY in the right panel
images.takeaway: The compass must open to more than half of XY, or the arcs will not meet.
images.description: Two panels: on the left short arcs from X and Y that never meet, on the right longer equal arcs that meet at A and B with the bisector drawn through them.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask why the left arcs miss each other, then try other radii in the practice to see which choices still work.

image_decisions.why: A side by side contrast shows the one radius rule that every later choice depends on.
